title: Postorder traversal of the root and its original children
summary: Walk two publicly constructed compilation units and compare each returned node by identity, in order, with the objects in the original tree.

change.description: Walk two publicly constructed compilation units and compare each returned node by identity, in order, with the objects in the original tree.

verdictLabel: Native 2/8 at original scope, 8/8 with observed LineSeparator startup, finite JVM 8/8
notes: With no application class captured and the caller supplying any separator through two UTF-16 units, all eight original traversal obligations have native decisions. Six held and the two parent counterexamples replayed on fresh JVMs. The absent-property and text-through-three-units controls cover the original enum as well. The ambient property still has no bound on its value or identity at ordinary entry. See verification/domain-foundations/expansion.json.
This is a conditional transfer case outside the six primary PRs. Guava's entry iterator carried the backing count through its nested frames and exhausted normally.
The independent original-scope grid has 2 inputs. Both revisions use the same declared receiver shapes.

Postorder findAll on an empty root threw EmptyStackException on the parent and returned the original root once on the fix. Both revisions preserved Name, PackageDeclaration, CompilationUnit order for package com, with receiver identity and preorder as controls.

The original ambient native run stopped at System.getProperty("line.separator") in LineSeparator initialization. The initial enum-only run retained its constants, names, ordinals and text and stopped at the printer configuration’s HashSet(Collection) constructor.

A separately scoped run initialized the original Node on JDK 21.0.13, bound its state digest, and compared 14 other classes with their state after independent initialization. All eight traversal and preservation obligations were decided under that condition. The empty-root postorder and terminal counterexamples also reproduced on the original parent without the startup condition. The other six original native obligations remain open.

The pilot traced both reads of line.separator and tested LF, CRLF, empty and a cleared property on both original JVM revisions. Clearing it before entry causes initialization failure from NullPointerException followed by NoClassDefFoundError on the next use. The field and consumer bytecode tables are in verification/domain-foundations/dependencies.

With only LineSeparator named as a startup root, the native checker now establishes six traversal contracts and refutes two on the parent. A separate caller sets or clears the property before first use. Both original revisions preserve the supplied raw reference and its escape description for every non-null string through three UTF-16 units, and a clear gives initializer failure followed by erroneous reuse. On both frozen trees and every supplied separator through two units, the fixed postorder holds and the parent empty-tree witness replays. These caller prestates are recorded separately from the six open ordinary claims in verification/domain-foundations/followup.json.
